about.what: Lesson A21's own settings: the levers' ranges, the assumptions of each stress test, the thresholds named on the page, the lever sort and the real-world context added to Prairieland's. Every Prairieland number (imports, stocks, minerals, the battery factory, the shocks, fuel prices, GDP, primary energy) is read from prairieland.json at run time, never copied here.

gasCut.what: gas use cut for the year (efficiency, electrification); LNG falls first, domestic output stays

weeks.what: how long the strait stays closed

stockDays.what: oil stocks, in days of net oil imports (the IEA's measure)

restraint.what: oil use cut during the closure (demand restraint)

cap.what: the most any one refiner supplies of each mineral, set before the restriction; the rest moves to the others in proportion

recycled.what: share of each mineral the factory gets from recycling at home

mineralDays.what: the factory's mineral stocks, in days of its use

split.what: share of the cell-making capacity at a second site

assume.gasStorageWhat: Gas storage is half full when the strait closes (set for teaching).
assume.spike: The price spike lasts the whole year; domestic gas output stays at its 2025 level, so a cut in gas use comes off LNG first.
assume.spikeStocks: More sellers do not remove exposure to a shared world price; stored gas can cushion purchases while it lasts, and this calculation models only using less.
assume.closure: Oil stocks are counted in days of net oil imports, as the IEA counts them; stocks cover the oil the closed strait stops, net of any demand restraint.
assume.ban: During the restriction, the other supply groups deliver only their usual shares and recycled material is domestic; nothing else is bought.
assume.fire: The fire stops the main site; a second site, if any, can run up to its full capacity.
assume.jobs: Jobs at each site in proportion to its capacity; job-years before any work elsewhere.
assume.parallel: The rows are separate stress tests: a cut in gas use lowers the LNG bill in a price spike, but not the LNG a closure stops.
assume.overlap: Combined, month by month: the factory makes what its scarcest mineral and its open sites allow, up to its 2025 output; minerals that arrive while it is shut wait in stock.
assume.overlapCount: Cells made after the restriction ends are not counted; the fire's timing matters only when the restriction is on too.
assume.set: teaching: every assumption in this block

thresholds.hhiWhat: The 2023 U.S. Merger Guidelines call a market with an HHI above 1,800 highly concentrated: a competition convention, not a security rule.
thresholds.oneCountryWhat: The EU's Critical Raw Materials Act sets a benchmark, not a legal cap: by 2030 no single third country should supply more than 65% of its yearly use of any strategic raw material, at any processing stage.

fireTimingWhat: When the fire starts inside the restriction: its first month, its middle, or its last months (computed from the two shocks' lengths in prairieland.json).

items.label: Stockpiles of oil, gas and minerals

why.spike: A stock release can ease a price spike, but a spike that lasts a year outlasts most stocks.
why.closure: Stocks bridge the weeks a route is closed.
why.ban: Mineral stocks keep the factory running while it finds other supply.
why.fire: Minerals in stock make no cells while the factory is down.

why.spike: A world price rise reaches every seller.
why.closure: Only suppliers that avoid the strait help.
why.ban: Others keep delivering when one country stops.
why.fire: The factory itself is the single point.

why.closure: The strait carries oil and LNG, not battery minerals.
why.ban: Recycled minerals cover only the recycled share of the need.
why.fire: The factory that uses the minerals is down.

why.spike: Cells do not change the price of gas.
why.closure: The strait carries oil and LNG.
why.ban: Both sites need the same minerals.
why.fire: One site keeps making cells while the other is rebuilt.

why.spike: Every unit not bought avoids the higher price.
why.closure: Less oil to replace while the strait is closed.
why.ban: On this page, using less changes gas and oil use only; the factory's mineral need stays the same.
